sentences.text: Lakhi Rani Das vs Jadumoni Konwar on 18 October, 2023

Bench: Surya Kant, Dipankar Datta
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No. 6859 Of 2023
 (Arising out of Slp (C) No. 23928 of 2023)
 (Arising out of Diary No. 16187 of 2020)
 Lakhi Rani Das ...Appel
 Vs.
 Jadumoni Konwar And Ors. ...Respo
 O R D E R

1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted.
3. Bimal Dasinjured claimant has filed this Appeal through his mother Smt. Lakhi Rani Das.

The injured claimant is aggrieved by the judgment dated 18.05.2018 passed by the Gauhati High Court,
granting him compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 after assessing the loss of earnings at the rate of Rs. 4,000/- per month.
The case of the appellant is that the injured claimant was a skilled workman who used to work as a pandal decorator and was earning Rs 10,000/- per month.
The claimant sustained an injury in a motor vehicle accident on 16.06.2008, as a result of which, he suffered 100% disability due to loss of

19:58:21 IST Reason:
vision in both eyes.

The factum of 100% disability suffered by Bimal Das in the accident is not in dispute and has been duly proved on record through Exts. 7, 8, 9, 10 and the disability certificate (Ext. 11), which has been issued by the Medical Officer of Tinsukia Civil Hospital.

The doctor from the said hospital has also been examined as witness No. 4 and he has testified the issuance of disability certificate (Ext. 11).
4.
The only short question that requires consideration pertains to the monthly income and consequential loss suffered by the injured claimantBimal Das.
5. While the Tribunal assessed the income of the claimant at the rate of Rs. 3,000/- per month, the High Court has increased the same to Rs. 4,000/- per month.
The appellant, on the other hand claims, that as a skilled worker, he used to earn Rs. 10,000/- per month.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

Taking into consideration the fact, that when the claimant met with an accident in the year 2008, it appears to us that the monthly income of the injured claimant for bare sustenance could not have been less than Rs. 200/- per day i.e., Rs. 6,000/- per month.

It might be true that the injured claimant could not have been earning the exact claimed amount of Rs. 10,000/- per month and the same could have varied from time to time depending upon his engagement as a pandal decorator.
Even while assuming that such a claim made by him was exaggerated, an unskilled worker at the relevant time cannot be accepted to earn less than Rs. 200 per day.

In undertaking this exercise of estimating the monthly income of the injured claimant, we are inclined to take a clue from the observations made by this Court in Laxmi Devi & Others vs. Mohammad Tabbar & Another; (2008) 12 SCC 165.

entities.text: Laxmi Devi & Others vs. Mohammad Tabbar & Another; (2008) 12 SCC 165
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That was a case where the wife of the deceased asserted that the deceased used to earn Rs. 140/- per day.
This Court observed that even if such a claim was slightly exaggerated, the daily income of Rs. 100/- per day could be expected as reasonable and fair.
On the contrary, the evidence on record in the instant case suggests that the injured claimant is a skilled workman who used to work as a pandal decorator.

Applying a similar yardstick to the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, we are satisfied that the daily earning of the injured claimant in the year 2008 must not have been less than Rs. 200/- per day i.e.,
Rs. 6,000/- per month.
7. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
The injured claimant (Bimal Das) is held entitled to enhanced compensation on the basis of loss of income of Rs. 6,000/- per month.
The rest of the compensation, as awarded by the High Court in para 16 of the impugned judgment, is kept intact.

Consequently, the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tinsukia is directed to recalculate the amount of compensation payable to the appellant on the basis of the injured claimants income at the rate of Rs. 6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal shall do the needful within one month.
The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the Insurance Company within two weeks thereafter.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
